The lion belongs to the genus Panthera..why: Textbook taxonomy, stated thousands of times with the binomial Panthera leo and in the lead of Wikipedia's Lion article.

sources.quote: The lion (Panthera leo) is a large cat of the genus Panthera

The genus Panthera includes the lion..why: The same fact from the genus's side: 'genus Panthera' and 'Panthera leo' are stated thousands of times, and Wikipedia's Lion article places the lion in the genus Panthera in its first sentence.

sources.quote: The lion (Panthera leo) is a large cat of the genus Panthera

The gray wolf belongs to the genus Canis.why: Textbook taxonomy, stated thousands of times with the binomial Canis lupus; Wikipedia's Canis article lists wolves in the genus.

sources.quote: Canis is a genus of the Caninae which includes multiple extant species, such as wolves, dogs, coyotes, and golden jackals.

The lion and the gray wolf belong to dif.why: Nobody compares the two genera; a model combines the lion in Panthera with the gray wolf in Canis. Both are stated thousands of times; the comparison itself was not counted (the counting service refused further requests while this record was written).

The lion is not a member of the family C.why: A negative nobody writes; a model gets it from the lion being in Panthera, a genus of cats (Felidae), not of dogs. The genus and binomial facts are common; the direct negative was not counted (counting service refused further requests).

Mosquitoes transmit malaria..why: Stated in the first sentence of Wikipedia's article.

sources.quote: Malaria is a mosquito-borne infectious disease that is transmitted by the bite of Anopheles mosquitoes.

Malaria is caused by a virus..why: False: malaria is caused by single-celled Plasmodium parasites, not a virus.

sources.quote: Malaria is caused by single-celled parasites of the genus Plasmodium, generally spread through the bites of an infected female Anopheles mosquito.

The genus of the lion, Panthera, belongs.why: Taxonomy texts give the lion's genus and the genus's family together: Wikipedia's Panthera article opens with 'a genus within the family Felidae' and names the lion among its species.

sources.quote: Panthera is a genus within the family Felidae, and one of two extant genera in the subfamily Pantherinae. It contains the largest living members of the cat family. There are five living species: the jaguar, leopard, lion, snow leopard and tiger.

sources.query: Panthera is a genus within the family Felidae

The animal known as the king of the jung.why: Nobody gives the genus through the nickname: a model resolves 'the king of the jungle' to the lion and then takes the lion's genus. The direct form is absent; the nickname and the genus are each common.

sources.query: the king of the jungle belongs to the genus Panthera
the king of the jungle, Panthera leo
the lion, the king of the jungle
the lion, the king of the jungle

The genus Canis belongs to the family Ca.why: Wolves, dogs and coyotes, the species of Canis, are the canids, as Wikipedia's Canis and Canidae articles say.

sources.quote: Canis is a genus of the Caninae which includes multiple extant species, such as wolves, dogs, coyotes, and golden jackals.
The Caninae are the canines, and include domestic dogs, wolves, coyotes, raccoon dogs, foxes, jackals, and other species.

sources.query: the genus Canis of the family Canidae
sources.note: Small: the fact is mostly stated through its species (wolves, dogs and coyotes are canids).

The species epithet in the lion's scient.why: The binomial Panthera leo is stated thousands of times.

A scientific name is the genus followed.why: True by the meaning of a binomial name: genus first, species epithet second.

notes: Stored edit (the lion's genus: in_genus, functional and inverse). Related near is the functional exclusion (Panthera no longer includes the lion), with the inverse as an alternative route; related far composes the edit with the family of the new genus, against the stored 'Panthera is a genus within the family Felidae'. Derived: composition (same genus as the gray wolf), inheritance as an application (the prompt says the field guide files each species under the family of its genus, so the answer cannot come from the lion's own stored family, Felidae) and binding (the king of the jungle). The one indeterminate query is the lion's scientific name (background beliefs): stored as a name of its own it stays Panthera leo, built from the genus it becomes Canis leo. It replaces the big-cat query, whose second world denied a firm fact, and the earlier 'scientific name' related-far question, which was the edit in other words. The earlier zoo-enclosure question was dropped: the lion's family is stored by name, so it was not determinate without the field-guide rule. Replaces the earlier plague-carrier edit. The zh answer uses the Chinese genus name; es uses the Latin name. Counts are exact-phrase counts in Dolma (v4_dolma-v1_7_llama).
